---
title: Embedded Interactive Computation
---

[Quarto Live](https://r-wasm.github.io/quarto-live/) embeds executable R and
Python cells directly in a Quarto page. The code runs in the reader's browser,
so a static website can provide editable examples, automated exercise feedback,
plots, and data analysis without a separate computation server.

Embedded cells are useful when an explanation needs more scaffolding than a
REPL, but a complete notebook environment would add unnecessary complexity.
For a notebook-style alternative, see the [JupyterLite example](jupyterlite.qmd).

## Examples

- [Scaffolded Python exercises](embedded_computation/python_exercises.qmd)
  develops a sequence around Himmelblau's function. It demonstrates setup
  cells, custom checks, targeted feedback, hints, solutions, optimization, and
  validation of a learner-created plot.
- [Analysing uploaded data](embedded_computation/data_upload.qmd) combines an
  Observable JavaScript file picker with Python running in the browser. Readers
  can upload an Excel workbook, validate it, calculate summary statistics, and
  plot the results without sending the file to a server.

## Installation

From the directory containing the Quarto project's `_quarto.yml`, run:

```default
pixi run quarto add r-wasm/quarto-live
```

This installs the extension below the project's `_extensions` directory. Enable
it for a page by selecting a Quarto Live HTML format in the YAML header:

```yaml
---
title: An interactive page
format: live-html
---
```

Projects that define their HTML theme and stylesheet centrally may need to
repeat those settings under `live-html`, as demonstrated in the example pages.
For a fuller introduction to authoring cells, see
[Interactive Python](../code_interactive/quarto-live-pyodide.qmd).

## Execution environments

Ordinary interactive cells share the global execution environment by default,
so a later cell can use definitions created by an earlier cell. Exercises are
isolated from one another to avoid accidental cross-talk. Setup cells marked
with `#| setup: true` provide definitions for the other cells belonging to the
same exercise.

See [Managing Environments](https://r-wasm.github.io/quarto-live/exercises/environments.html)
for details.

## Connecting OJS and embedded computation

Quarto Live cells can consume reactive values created by Observable JavaScript
(OJS). List the OJS variable names under the cell's `input` option:

```python
#| input:
#|   - selected_value
```

When `selected_value` changes, Quarto Live passes the new value into the
browser-based R or Python environment and reevaluates the cell. This makes OJS
controls—including file selectors—useful front ends for embedded analysis.
Quarto Live performs automatic conversion between common JavaScript, R, and
Python data types; binary files can be transferred as arrays of bytes.

See the Quarto Live documentation on
[reactivity with OJS](https://r-wasm.github.io/quarto-live/interactive/reactivity.html)
and [data conversion](https://r-wasm.github.io/quarto-live/interactive/data.html).
